title: Chicken and Mushroom Pasty
subtitle: A shortcrust pasty filled with chicken and chestnut mushrooms in a creamy sauce
excerpt: Tender chicken and earthy chestnut mushrooms in a creamy sauce, enclosed in a crisp shortcrust parcel. Good hot for lunch or packed cold for work.
sourceNotes: British pasty tradition with a chicken and mushroom filling, adapted from classic short-pastry baking methods.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked and cooled pasties individually. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 20 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half. The filling can be made the day before.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling the day before and refrigerate. Assemble and bake when needed.

content.text: These pasties have a creamy chicken and mushroom filling inside a short, buttery pastry. The filling must be properly cooled before it goes into the pastry. A wet or warm filling will make the base go soft.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the chicken cubes for 4 minutes until just cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until they give up their liquid. Stir in the thyme.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables. Stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the stock and milk, stirring to make a thick sauce. Season well.
Return the chicken to the pan. Stir to combine. Spread the filling onto a plate and leave to cool completely.

Heat the oven to 200C. Divide the pastry into four. Roll each piece into a circle about 20cm across. Spoon filling onto one half of each circle. Brush the edges with beaten egg, fold over and crimp firmly.
Place on the lined baking tray. Chill for 20 minutes. Brush with beaten egg and cut a small slit in each.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep gold. Rest for 5 minutes before eating.

items.symptom: The filling leaks out during baking.
items.cause: The edges were not sealed firmly or the filling was too liquid.
items.fix: Crimp the edge firmly and make sure the sauce is thick before filling. Chilling the assembled pasty helps.

items.symptom: The pastry is pale after 40 minutes.
items.cause: The egg glaze was too thin or the oven was not hot enough.
items.fix: Add a second coat of egg glaze and bake for a further 5 minutes.

items.cause: The chicken was overcooked in the frying pan before it went into the pastry.
items.fix: Cook the chicken just until the pink is gone. It will finish cooking inside the pasty during baking.
